latest.name: CodeRabbit — AI Code Review
latest.short_verdict: A PR-focused AI code reviewer, not another code-completion copilot. Its public-repository/open-source plan is free indefinitely and includes AI pull-request reviews. Public repos with fewer than 10 stars must trigger reviews manually; OSS rate limits apply, but the official pages reviewed do not publish a fixed numeric quota.
latest.what_it_does: Reviews proposed code changes in GitHub and GitLab pull requests using codebase context. It flags possible bugs, edge cases, security and quality issues; explains diffs; and can provide PR summaries, slop detection, triage, Change Stack and security reviews. It also offers CLI and IDE review workflows. This is a review/validation stage after code is written, distinct from GitHub Copilot Free's primary code-completion and in-editor assistance use case.
latest.why_try_it: Useful as an independent first-pass reviewer before merging changes, especially when code was written with an AI coding assistant or when a solo developer has no second reviewer. The public-repository offer is genuinely free without a card, so an eligible public project can test the workflow on real pull requests.
latest.free_tier: CodeRabbit's Open Source offer is $0 for public repositories, free indefinitely. Official pages say public repositories receive AI code reviews and OSS access to Team-level features including slop detection, triage, Change Stack and security reviews on pull requests. Sign up with GitHub or GitLab and install the app on a public repository; no application or credit card is required. For public repositories with fewer than 10 stars, reviews must be triggered manually using the CodeRabbit status comment or @coderabbitai review. The vendor says OSS rate limits apply, but the official pages reviewed do not publish an exact numeric monthly or hourly quota.
latest.limits: The free OSS offer requires a public repository; private repositories are not covered by this offer and require a paid plan after any trial. OSS-specific rate limits apply, and the exact numeric cap was not published in the official pages reviewed. Repositories with fewer than 10 stars require manual review triggering. AI findings can be wrong or incomplete and must be checked by a human and normal tests; do not auto-merge solely on its verdict. Privacy caveat: CodeRabbit's Privacy Notice says OSS review data is excluded from its no-training representation and may be used to train its systems; it also stores some review-improvement data such as vector embeddings, with an opt-out. Full-codebase Deep Scans and some on-demand products may have separate usage pricing.
latest.signup_pakistan: No Pakistan-specific exclusion was found in the public Terms of Use reviewed; they grant worldwide access subject to applicable local law, sanctions and export-control rules. Signup requires connecting a GitHub or GitLab account. The public-repository OSS offer does not require a payment card. Pakistan-based signup was not independently tested, and acceptance of Pakistan-issued cards for paid plans was not verified.
latest.quality_evidence: Independent evidence: the live Martian Code Review Bench checked 2026-11-13 showed CodeRabbit at #5 with F1 61.3%, precision 69.8% and recall 54.6%; it is a continuously updated benchmark, not a permanent ranking or guarantee. Vendor-reported adoption: CodeRabbit said it completed 1,049,817 open-source reviews in September 2026 and was installed on 300,000+ public repositories; the review count includes repeat reviews of the same PR. GitHub Marketplace showed a verified publisher and 369,621 installs. Anecdotal feedback is mixed: one Reddit developer described a privacy/logic flaw caught during review, while Trustpilot showed only 10 reviews and a 2.1/5 score with recent complaints about paid-plan billing and rate limits; this small, self-selected sample is not representative.
latest.android_status: No official CodeRabbit Android app was verified in Google Play searches. The primary product is a web application and GitHub/GitLab integration, with separate CLI and IDE workflows. Unrelated third-party apps using similar names are not official CodeRabbit apps.
